static_traits.name: Han Li
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of friends and family, can confide in them when encountering difficulties, but has not yet discussed this sense of incompetence and Self-doubt with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of psychological counseling or treatment before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe experiences and automatic thoughts concretely; negative attitude, tending toward catastrophizing and self-deprecation; repeatedly replaying accident memories; cooperativeness Good

basic_info.main_problem: After falling off the bike twice this week, developing incompetence feelings related to cycling, inadequacy and Self-doubt, affecting confidence and emotions, and progressing to avoiding cycling and related activities.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent feelings of incompetence and Self-doubt affecting overall well-being and hindering enjoyment of activities like cycling; hoping to lessen these negative feelings, Recovering confidence, enjoying cycling again.

special_situations.event: Falling off the bike twice in a row this week
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I keep making mistakes in a short time, it proves I will never learn to cycle/I am just not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stopping cycling, avoiding related activities, trying self-comfort but ineffectively
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible, I will never ride well

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking about cycling or recalling the crash
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try again there will definitely be another accident; I must avoid it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding getting in the car and practicing, procrastinating

special_situations.event: Social activities involving cycling or the outdoors / talking about cycling with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform badly, others will judge or not understand me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding cycling or outdoor activities with friends, Reduced socializing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not understand, will only tell me to 'hurry up and Recover'

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only zero mistakes counts as knowing how to ride; smooth rides do not count, only failure reveals the problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive evidence to maintain self-vigilance, continuing Self-doubt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those smooth rides were just luck, only crashes show I am not good enough

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and accepted, and to confirm oneself is capable and in control
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure exposing incompetence, being negated by others or self-worth collapsing
defense_goal: Lowers the feeling of failure and shame by avoiding cycling and related social activities
Attributing responsibility to oneself to maintain a sense of control, relieving Anxiety brought by uncertainty

object_relations.self_representation: incompetent, a failure who makes mistakes easily

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes that external factors (such as slippery roads) may also have an influence and invites considering multiple explanations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing attributing some causes to outside equals making excuses for one's incompetence, worrying about being seen as shirking
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use self-blaming statements to emphasize 'I should have handled it better/It is all my problem', tone resolute, ignoring external factors.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether feelings have been shared with friends or family and support sought
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Preset that others will negate or brush one off (believing they will not understand)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use speculative expressions ('they might/probably'), refusing to try communicating, tone defensive, reserved.

manifestations: Interest in the once-loved cycling and outdoor activities declines
Successful cycling experiences are ignored or devalued, making it hard to gain a sense of value from the activity
outcomes: Avoiding activities, Decreased sense of life satisfaction

manifestations: Restricts choices out of fear, avoids cycling and activities requiring balance / coordination
Attributing all responsibility to oneself, experiencing being bound by Anxiety and self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently Self-doubting in sessions, using expressions like 'I am not good enough/I should be better'
Holds a cautious attitude toward trying change; maintains a sense of control through self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Inferring friends or family 'will not understand, will only tell me to hurry up and Recover', therefore not communicating with them

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking about cycling or facing cycling activities with friends, the client usually develops intense Fear and Self-doubt, thus avoiding getting on the bike and practicing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a past smooth ride, he skillfully navigated around obstacles and felt in control, the whole ride went smoothly, with no intense Fear and Self-doubt appearing.
exception_events.reason: Clue: being focused on operating at the time, noticing one's ability to handle obstacles, experiencing self-efficacy; attention not yet dominated by Catastrophizing.

positive_force: Has supportive friends and family, which can serve as potential support resources
Has past experience of smooth cycling and feeling in control; positive evidence of capability
Work functioning stable, professional Self-efficacy not yet affected
Willing to try challenging negative thinking and expresses the motivation 'want to enjoy cycling again'
Able to identify and express inner thoughts and emotions, fairly good Reflection ability
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and overgeneralization are significant
Repeatedly replaying the accident, Reinforcing self-blame and feelings of incompetence
Avoids cycling and related socializing, forming a negative cycle
Negative predictions and mind reading about others, reducing the use of external support
Negating positive experiences, attention biased toward the negative

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids cycling and activities involving balance/coordination
antecedent: Thinking about cycling or recalling crashing scenes
Invited to cycling or outdoor activities with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Forming the core belief 'I am incompetent' after consecutive crashes, accompanied by catastrophic and black-and-white thinking, worrying about failing and getting injured again
target_behavior.function: Avoiding perceived danger and possible failure/shame, lowering Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased interest, damaged emotions, missing positive experiences and ability-Recovery opportunities, Social avoidance

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly replaying crash scenes and self-deprecating automatic thoughts (such as 'I am terrible' 'I will never get better')
antecedent: Repeatedly recalling the accident after the second fall
Thinking about cycling when Being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Trying to gain control and Interpretation through continuous review, influenced by overgeneralization and personalization, deepening confirmation bias about incompetence
target_behavior.function: Seeking illusory control of certainty and preventing future errors
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening Anxiety and depressive-like emotions, damaging confidence and motivation, maintaining avoidance behaviors
